correctness.rationale: The independent reconstruction /workspace/branches/a64cb395-fdff-44ff-9696-ea9ff56b91ce/independent_pappus_check.py checks the exact 18-vertex LCF graph, all faces at scale two, 99 Morse pairs and the topological sort of all 225 faces through 558 covers. Acyclicity and the one vertex and 26 critical triangles give a wedge of 26 two-spheres over the integers. The six distance-four classes give the actual six-factor join at scale three, hence 64 five-spheres and a top integral lattice of six tensored reduced H_0 factors. Permuting augmented join factors contributes the block-permutation sign, and the trace along each permuted tensor cycle is the composite three-point permutation's fixed-point count minus one. A complete independent 216-element enumeration reproduces both character histograms and matches the join trace elementwise to the signed chain trace. The character sums in degrees one, two and five are 0, 0 and 216; rational averaging after subdivision gives vanishing and rank-one quotient homology as claimed. The graph at scale one has rank 27-18+1=10, scale zero has 18 points, and scale four is a simplex. Integer distances and the reduced groups in distinct successive degrees give exactly the half-open intervals over every field. This does not establish integral quotient homology or equivariant homotopy types.

evidence: For general q>=3 the affine-plane deletion theorem gives the integral Rips types and barcodes and explicitly specializes to the 18-vertex Pappus graph at q=3. Adamaszek's cited scale-two girth comparison requires girth at least seven and the C_6-free criterion also excludes Pappus. The inspected hypercube papers concern a different graph family, including equivariant homology under the hyperoctahedral group.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Only the affine-plane theorem here covers the nonequivariant Pappus data; its general homotopy and persistence statements do not by themselves give the full 216-element characters.
